question.prompt: Let \(S\) be a set of \(6\) integers taken from \(\{1, 2, \ldots, 12\}\) with the property that if \(a\) and \(b\) are elements of \(S\) with \(a \lt b,\) then \(b\) is not a multiple of \(a.\) What is the least possible value of an element of \(S?\)

solutions.title: Rule out smaller minimum elements
solutions.explanation:
Test the possible smallest elements in order. Once a number belongs to \(S\), none of its larger multiples can belong to \(S\).

- If the smallest element is \(1\), every other number is forbidden, so \(S\) cannot have six elements.
- If it is \(2\), the only available numbers are \(2,3,5,7,9,11\). But \(3\) and \(9\) cannot both be chosen, leaving at most five elements.
- If it is \(3\), the only available numbers are \(3,4,5,7,8,10,11\). At most one of \(4,8\) and at most one of \(5,10\) can be chosen. These are two disjoint pairs, so at least two of the seven numbers must be omitted, again leaving at most five.

Thus the smallest element must be at least \(4\). This bound is attained by
\[
S=\{4,6,7,9,10,11\}.
\]
The larger multiples of \(4\) within the allowed range are \(8\) and \(12\), and the only larger multiple of \(6\) is \(12\); none is selected. Every other selected number exceeds \(6\), so its larger multiples exceed \(12\).

Therefore the least possible element is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
